settings.name_in_paper: Contextual causal bandits with non-manipulable variables (Bayesian formulation)
unmapped: Known causal graph without latent confounders; arms are interventions from POMISs of the projected graph with non-manipulable variables
Learner observes reward and all non-intervened variables after each intervention (richer than bandit feedback)
Unknown parameter is the set of CPTs with independent Dirichlet priors (parameter independence)
Contexts are ancestrally closed, observed before action; need not be exogenous (may carry information about theta)
Regret is against the context-dependent oracle mapping Pi*(c)
settings.definition_quote: We study contextual causal bandits with non-manipulable variables, where context variables are observed before action selection and additional variables are observed after each intervention. Assuming a known causal graph without latent confounding, we adopt a Bayesian formulation in which the conditional probability tables of the observational distribution constitute the unknown parameter.

algorithms.name: Thompson Sampling for causal bandits with non-manipulable variables (Algorithm 1)
Information-Directed Sampling for Causal Bandits with Non-Manipulable Variables (Algorithm 2, Monte Carlo)
IDS with oracle access (exact information ratio)

symbols.Gamma: uniform upper bound on the information-ratio coefficients Gamma_t
symbols.H_Pi: prior entropy of the optimal-action mapping Pi*

source.label: thm1
source.quote: The mean cumulative Bayesian regret of Algorithm~\ref{alg: thom} is bounded for any $T \in \mathbb{N}$ as follows, where $\Gamma \geq \Gamma_t$ for all $t \in \{1,\ldots,T\}$: \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T (Y_{\Pi^\star(\mathbf{C}_t),t} - Y_{A_t,t})] \leq \Gamma \sqrt{H(\Pi^\star) \, T}.

results.notes: Prior-dependent (entropy) Bayesian regret bound; regret defined on realized rewards in expectation, which equals Bayesian regret.

conditions: context space C is finite with |C| = M_ctx
K = |A| is the number of POMIS-induced interventions

source.label: crr_reg
source.quote: Suppose that the context space $\mathcal{C}$ is finite. The mean cumulative Bayesian regret for Algorithm~\ref{alg: thom} is bounded for any $T \in \mathbb{N}$ as follows: ... \leq \sqrt{\frac{T|\mathcal{A}| |\mathcal{C}|\log\!|\mathcal{A}|}{2}}.

results.notes: Uses Gamma_t^2 <= |A|/2 and H(Pi*) <= |C| log|A|. Proof also gives intermediate sqrt(|A|/2 H(Pi*) T).

symbols.H_Pi: prior entropy of the optimal-action mapping Pi*
symbols.G_sum: sum_{t=1}^T E[gamma_t 1_{E_t}], where gamma_t is the sup deviation of the information ratio over Monte Carlo confidence sets
symbols.delta_p: overall confidence level delta' of the Monte Carlo confidence bounds

tuning: N posterior Monte Carlo samples per round

source.label: thm2
source.quote: Fix $\delta'\in(0,1)$ and $T\in\mathbb{N}$. For each $t$, let $\mathcal{E}_t$ denote the event that the confidence bounds in Lemmas~\ref{lemm_2} and~\ref{lemm_gt_conc} hold for all $a\in\mathcal{A}$ at round $t$, using $\delta=\delta'/(2T|\mathcal{A}|)$. Then $\mathbb{P}(\cap_{t=1}^T\mathcal{E}_t)\geq1-\delta'$, and \mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^{T}(Y_{\Pi^\star(\mathbf{C}_t),t}-Y_{A_t,t})]\leq\sqrt{H(\Pi^\star)(\frac{T|\mathcal{A}|}{2}+2\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb{E}[\gamma_t\mathbbm{1}_{\mathcal{E}_t}])}+\delta'

results.notes: Bound may be vacuous if gamma_t = +infinity. Compute: paper states O(NK) Monte Carlo cost plus O(K^2) pair optimization per round ignoring model-dependent reward evaluation cost.

symbols.H_Pi: prior entropy of the optimal-action mapping Pi*

conditions: Delta_t(a|c_t) and g_t(a|c_t) computed exactly and exact information ratio minimized

source.label: cor:oracle
source.quote: Suppose that $\Delta_t(a\mid\mathbf{c}_t)$ and $g_t(a\mid\mathbf{c}_t)$ can be computed exactly at every round and IDS minimizes the exact information ratio. Then, for any $T\in\mathbb{N}$, the mean cumulative regret satisfies ... \leq \sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{A}|}{2}\,T\,H(\Pi^\star)}.

results.notes: Oracle IDS; follows standard Russo & Van Roy IDS analysis.

cited_results.setting_description: Causal bandit where intervention-induced distribution P(Pa_Y | a) is known; Y has n parents with k values each; Bayesian regret
